item.title: Real Madrid concerned about JJ Gabriel’s entourage despite imminent transfer
item.description: Real Madrid concerned about JJ Gabriel’s entourage despite imminent transfer Real Madrid have identified a potential complication related to the signing of Manchester United youngster JJ Gabriel, with concerns emerging over the influence of the teenager’s family and representatives. According to Mundo Deportivo , the club’s management are particularly attentive to the role played by his father, Joe O’Cearuill, as they prepare to bring the 16-year-old to Valdebebas. As stated before, the transfer is approaching its final stages , with Real Madrid expected to pay Manchester United approximately €360,000 in training compensation. However, while the Spanish giants are convinced by Gabriel’s potential, managing the people influencing his career could become an important part of the recruitment process. JJ Gabriel’s father raises concerns within Real Madrid It is to be noted that Gabriel’s father, Joe O’Cearuill, is a former professional footballer who represented the Republic of Ireland internationally. His involvement in his son’s development has attracted considerable attention throughout the transfer saga, particularly after disagreements emerged between the family and Manchester United. Real Madrid are concerned about the people influencing JJ Gabriel. (Photo by Naomi Baker/Getty Images) Reports in England have previously described O’Cearuill as a demanding influence when decisions concerning his son’s future are involved. Understandably so, some Real Madrid officials are concerned about the extent of his involvement. To understand the context, some background is relevant because Gabriel’s departure from Manchester United happened after disagreements grew over his involvement with the senior side. The teenager ultimately requested to leave in September, bringing an end to his six-year association with the English club. Real Madrid are aware that securing Gabriel’s signature is only one part of the challenge, while ensuring that he remains focused on football will also matter as he enters a new environment. Ali Barat’s appointment could help Real Madrid JJ Gabriel will sign a three-year deal with Real Madrid. (Photo by Alex Livesey/Getty Images) One development that could ease Real Madrid’s concerns is Gabriel’s decision to appoint Ali Barat as his representative through Epic Sports. The change in representation came shortly before his expected move to Spain and has been viewed as an important step towards completing the transfer. Barat already has established relationships with Real Madrid through his work with players such as Dean Huijsen and Denzel Dumfries. All this means his involvement has been particularly instrumental in moving negotiations forward, with the agent personally handling discussions surrounding Gabriel’s future. As far as the player is concerned, he will sign a three-year deal with Los Blancos , who will hope that the situation that caught Manchester United red-faced is not repeated at Valdebebas.

item.title: ‘I Don’t Think He’s in Great Shape,’ ‘I Need 25 and 10 From Him’ — NBA Legend Calls Out Bam Adebayo’s Conditioning, Demands More From Heat Star
item.description: ‘I Don’t Think He’s in Great Shape,’ ‘I Need 25 and 10 From Him’ — NBA Legend Calls Out Bam Adebayo’s Conditioning, Demands More From Heat Star Kevin Garnett isn’t satisfied with Bam Adebayo’s start to the 2026-27 NBA season. Even with the Miami Heat riding a six-game winning streak, the Hall of Famer took aim at the 29-year-old center’s conditioning and motor, questioning why playing alongside newly acquired superstar Giannis Antetokounmpo hasn’t pushed his game to another level. Speaking on “The KG and Stephen A. Show” on Thursday, Garnett challenged Adebayo to raise his nightly production and set a steeper physical standard for a Miami squad trying to contend in the Eastern Conference. Kevin Garnett Questions Bam Adebayo’s Conditioning Amid Heat’s Resurgence While Adebayo remains a key part of Heat coach Erik Spoelstra’s defense, Garnett was blunt when breaking down the three-time All-Star’s inconsistent early-season effort. “I need that every night. I need 25 and 10 from him. He’s young, he has a motor. I don’t think he’s in great shape, I don’t think he’s running hard, I don’t think he sprints and gets easy baskets,” Garnett said . “I thought being around Giannis, he would actually activate another level in him. But I’m watching him, man. He’s one of my favorites to watch, so I’m watching him with how he can be better.” Garnett’s critique carries extra sting given Miami’s notoriously strict fitness standards under team president Pat Riley and Spoelstra, which prioritize conditioning. But it isn’t the first time the Minnesota Timberwolves legend has called out Adebayo this season. After the Heat’s 131-106 opening-night loss to Minnesota, Garnett said on “KG Certified” that 13 to 15 points isn’t superstar production and that Adebayo needed to post 25 and 12 a night. The numbers back up Garnett’s concern to a degree. Through 15 appearances this season, Adebayo is averaging 18.9 points, 7.7 rebounds, and 3.1 assists on 52.4% shooting from the field and 24.5% from deep. It’s a noticeable dip from the 20.1 ppg and 10.0 rpg he put up during the 2025-26 campaign. Adebayo’s shot volume has also dipped to 12.3 attempts per game, down from 15.7. But last season, the Heat star also exploded for 83 points against the Washington Wizards, the second-highest single-game total in NBA history. That performance raised expectations for Adebayo, and Garnett’s 25-and-10 ask now looks like the floor. Still, the 6-foot-9 center has flashed the ceiling Garnett is asking for. The 10-year veteran erupted for 37 points and 14 rebounds in Miami’s 133-121 NBA Cup win over the Cleveland Cavaliers on Nov. 13 and poured in 26 points to help take down Antetokounmpo’s former squad, the Milwaukee Bucks, in Wednesday’s 137-130 victory. Now in the first year of a three-year, $160.3 million extension, Adebayo is earning $49.5 million this season and carries max-contract expectations alongside one of the league’s most dominant forces, Antetokounmpo. item.title: Defense key for Fort Defiance as team works to win state championship
item.description: Amber Pitsenbarger knew it was a cliche, but to her it's the truth. "Defense wins championships," the Fort Defiance volleyball coach said. If she's learned anything from her two previous trips to the state championship game, both losses by Fort Defiance, it's the importance of defense. Last year in a four-set loss to Radford in the title game, Pitsenbarger said Radford defenders did such a good job of digging up everything Fort was hitting at them. And that defense forced a lot of hitting errors by Fort Defiance. This year the coach wants Fort to be that team that is digging up everything. When her team takes the court she is hoping to be the team forcing errors, not making them. Region 2B champion Fort Defiance (24-2) will play Region 2D runner-up John Battle (20-13) at noon Nov. 21 in Salem for the Class 2 state championship. While it's Fort's third straight trip to the state championship game, Battle hasn't been to the finals since 1999. "Honestly, it has been an incredible experience," Battle coach Sydney McKinney said of this year's run to the championship game. "When I took over this program, getting to this point was something I hoped we could accomplish, but to actually see it happen is very special." Battle's one-and-only appearance in the state championship game was 1999 when it lost to Wilson Memorial. But this year's team, despite a record with double digit losses, believes it can win a state title. Seven of its losses came in a multi-day tournament in early September against tough competition. Three other losses came against Ridgeview, the team Battle finally beat in the state semifinals to advance to Saturday's match. They also split with Abingdon, which is playing for the Class 3 state championship, and swept Patrick Henry Glade Spring, which is in the Class 1 state title match. So they have been tested. McKinney said the tough schedule was intentional, a way to challenge themselves. The difficult situations that they found themselves in during those matches forced the team to adjust and learn to compete under pressure, something the coach feels like will help in the ultimate pressure match Saturday. "That tournament especially gave us an opportunity to see where we needed to improve," McKinney said. "You learn a lot about your team when you play against tough competition, and those experiences have helped us become more comfortable in high-pressure situations." Fort Defiance has been tested this season as well. Last year the team was undefeated heading into the state championship game, sweeping all but two of its matches before running into Radford. This season, Fort lost to both Turner Ashby and Wilson Memorial and went to five sets against Wilson in the first meeting between the teams. Both Turner Ashby and Wilson reached the postseason in Class 3, with Wilson getting to the state tournament. item.description: Leeds United v Manchester United - Pre-Season Friendly - Getty Images Sport Real Madrid are close to finalizing a major coup in the youth market as they prepare to welcome JJ Gabriel to the Santiago Bernabeu. The 16-year-old talent has already said his goodbyes to Manchester United, but one final bureaucratic hurdle remains before he can officially pull on the famous white shirt. The final hurdle for Real Madrid The long-running saga surrounding Gabriel’s future is reaching its conclusion as the teenager prepares to swap Manchester for Madrid . While terms have been fully agreed between the player and the Spanish giants, the transfer cannot be officially registered until football’s global governing body, FIFA, provides the necessary clearance. This step is a standard but essential requirement for all international transfers involving players who are under the age of 18. Madrid have been meticulous in their approach to this deal, ensuring all legal requirements were met to avoid any potential complications with the governing body's strict regulations on minor transfers. The club remains confident that there will be no issues in securing the final authorization. The player has already taken significant steps toward his new life in Spain, having recently visited the club’s Valdebebas facilities to meet the staff and teammates he will soon be working alongside on a daily basis. Gabriel has already confirmed his departure from Old Trafford with a message to the Premier League giants. Writing on social media, the youngster stated: "Goodbye and thank you, Man United," as quoted by AS . Training schedule and contract details The agreement between the two parties is set to span three years, which is the maximum duration permitted for youth players under current footballing statutes. Although he cannot feature in official matches until the paperwork is fully processed and the registration window opens, Gabriel has already begun maintaining his fitness in the Spanish capital. He is currently training in Boadilla del Monte, located in the north of Madrid, to ensure he is ready for the demands of the Spanish game. Madrid view Gabriel as a long-term investment and have a clear pathway mapped out for his growth within their prestigious academy system. The initial plan involves him working with the youth teams to adapt to the club's specific tactical requirements and culture. Given the excitement surrounding his arrival, there is significant anticipation from both the club and Spanish football observers to see how he translates his potential into performances on the pitch. item.title: Hillsdale Academy’s Cote, Apel earn all-region volleyball honors
item.description: HILLSDALE — Two Hillsdale Academy volleyball seniors earned postseason recognition following a season that saw the Colts capture their fourth consecutive district championship. More: Jonesville ends historic football season, our favorite moments Seniors Lucy Cote and Malorie-Kate Apel were selected for all-region honors by the Michigan Interscholastic Volleyball Coaches Association (MIVCA) after leading coach Katherine Huffman’s squad to a 23-9 overall record. Cote was the Colts’ leading offensive threat throughout the 2026 campaign. The senior middle hitter finished the season with a team-high 355 kills and 83 blocks. She averaged 3.9 kills per set while also contributing 255 digs and 43 aces. Apel anchored the Colts’ back-row defense, recording a team-high 398 digs and 455 serve receptions. The senior libero averaged 4.4 digs per set and finished second on the team with 62 aces. Both seniors also earned first-team all-league and SCAA dream team honors. Fellow senior Zoe Plemmons joined the duo as a first-team all-league selection after recording 192 kills and 326 digs this season. Colts cap season with fourth straight district title Hillsdale Academy secured its fourth consecutive Division 4 district championship with a four-set victory over Pittsford before seeing its postseason run come to an end against Fulton on Tuesday, Nov. 10. The Colts twice battled back from a set deficit in the regional semifinal before falling to the Pirates in five sets, 22-25, 25-19, 13-25, 25-23 and 10-15. Cote finished her final high school volleyball match with 19 kills, 19 digs and five blocks, while Apel led the defense with 24 digs. Plemmons added seven kills and 12 digs. Freshman setter Lucy Molenkamp recorded 36 assists. Hillsdale Academy will graduate five seniors from its latest district championship team: Ava Lutz, Cote, Maribelle Jennings, Plemmons and Apel. item.title: Pittsford's Alexis Bryner earns all-region honors
item.description: PITTSFORD — Pittsford junior Alexis Bryner earned all-region honors from the Michigan Interscholastic Volleyball Coaches Association (MIVCA) after leading the Wildcats to their best season since 2022. More: Jonesville ends historic football season, our favorite moments Bryner, a three-year varsity athlete and team co-captain this fall, helped coach Jessica Butler’s squad finish with a 21-12 overall record and a Division 4, district runner-up finish. The junior led the Wildcats in kills in every match this season, accumulating 396 kills, 33 blocks, 210 digs and 50 aces across 89 sets played. She averaged 4.4 kills per set. Bryner’s ability to contribute in all six rotations and the power behind her attacks made her a consistent offensive threat for the Wildcats. “She is a great athlete, strong, hard worker, and I am excited to have her returning for another season — her senior year,” Butler said. Bryner also earned first-team all-league and Southern Central Athletic Association dream team honors alongside fellow junior teammate Karmin Butler. The Wildcats’ postseason run came to an end in a four-set loss to Hillsdale Academy in the District 119 championship game. This season, the Wildcats played in honor of Sara Bryner, Alexis and Layla Bryner's grandmother, who was honored at the 2026 Jonesville "I Wear Pink for Someone Special" volleyball tournament. With just one senior graduating from this year’s squad and two dream team selections eligible to return, Lizzy Bump, Pittsford will bring back much of the talent that helped the program reach the district final as it looks to build on its 21-win campaign in 2027. item.title: Penn State football prediction, getting Rutgers at the right time
item.description: It may well be the perfect time for this Penn State football team to play the Rutgers Scarlet Knights . The Nittany Lions are preparing for their first Senior Day game under coach Matt Campbell on Saturday, Nov. 21, in Beaver Stadium. They're riding a three-game winning streak with marked improvements to their running game , quarterback play and pass rush. They've not committed a turnover in a month. The Scarlet Knights? They're a mess at 2-8 (1-6 in the Big Ten), having lost their most dynamic playmaker to injury (KJ Duff). They're struggling to score with backup quarterbacks and are getting pummeled on defense. They've lost four straight, only one of them close. The Lions have never lost to Rutgers in 11 meetings since joining the Big Ten. Penn State football vs. Rutgers key to the game The matchup of the day should be Rutgers star running back Antwan Raymond against the PSU linebackers, particularly All-America Tony Rojas and improving Kooper Ebel. Raymond's one of the best in the Big Ten and, truly enough, the Knights' main hope to stay in this early. He ran for 150 yards against Northwestern in October and tore up Penn State in last year's regular-season finale, going for 189 yards on the ground and 22 more on receptions. Penn State vs. Rutgers scouting report The Lions have consistently jumped on opponents for early leads, which could potentially bury this Rutgers team. The Knights have yielded 31 points or more in six of their past seven Big Ten games. They don't offer much on offense, either, beyond the splendid running of Raymond. In last week's loss to Nebraska, their two backup quarterbacks, subbing for injured starter Dylan Lonergan, combined for only 42 passing yards on seven completions with two interceptions. It's not a good script against a Penn State team that has improved its efficiency and production significantly over the past month. That starts in the red zone, where the Lions have scored touchdowns on nine of their 10 opportunities during their streak. Look for another big day from the PSU tailbacks, even if injured Carson Hansen can't go. Penn State vs. Rutgers score prediction Penn State 45, Rutgers 10 Frank Bodani covers Penn State football for the York Daily Record and USA Today Network. item.title: Bovair named Monroe County Region Boys Cross Country Coach of the Year
item.description: CARLETON – Who needs a star? Apparently not Mark Bovair and Airport’s boys cross country team. Bovair called it “unique” when Airport’s boys cross country team won the Huron League championship last year without a single runner qualifying individually for the state finals. His Jets are making unique common. Flashback to 2025: Airport's Mark Bovair named Monroe County Region Boys Cross Country Coach of the Year They repeated as league champs this fall, despite losing last year’s top runner. “It’s difficult to win without a real superstar in the lineup, but we figured out a way,” Bovair said. In addition to repeating as league champs, Airport took second in its regional and placed 25th at the Division 2 state finals. Bovair has been named Monroe County Region Boys Cross Country Coach of the Year for the second straight season. “We do it a little unconventionally,” Bovair said. “My philosophy is that cross country is 100-percent a team sport. It’s the greatest team sport there is. “You need contributions from everyone. You can’t hide. Everyone has to be all-in.” That philosophy became reality in the first Huron League jamboree of the season. New Boston Huron and Airport tied for first place with 58 points, but Airport won a tiebreaker when its sixth runner Jacob Kuti finished ahead of Huron’s sixth man. In fact, the Jets had three runners in front of the No. 6 runner for Huron. “We tell every runner that they count,” Bovair said. “And, on that day, every runner did count.” Airport’s magic did not work in the second jamboree with Huron winning 60-65. “In the second one, they came out strong and really took it to us,” Bovair said. The split of the first two jamborees meant that the winner of the league championship meet would walk away with the overall title. Bovair had his runners seeing red, as in the red uniforms of Huron. “Everyone had a job,” Bovair said. “I told them, ‘You’re not going to catch Christian (individual winner Christian Craanen of St. Mary Catholic Central) or the other guys in front.’ They just had to get as close as they could to Huron’s runners to save us points.” The pack mentality worked perfectly as Hunter Rodak, Kuti, Andrew Bell, Axel Thompson, Grady Marino, Hayden Bovair and Jenson Wright ran 7-8-12-14-15-21-32 and Airport topped Huron 56-63. “It’s really satisfying when you put plan in place and it works,” Bovair said. Even Bovair had doubts about the plan in the Division 2 regional at Lake Erie Metropark on Halloween morning. “I don’t know if it works or not at bigger meets,” he admitted. “It’s hard when you don’t get a runner in the top 10.” But Airport did crack the top 10 twice that day with Rodak claiming eighth and Bell 10th. item.description: Cricket Australia prepares to stand by Pat Cummins despite Cameron Bancroft's Sandpapergate revelations originally appeared on Cricket News . Cummins has told senior officials he wants to stay in the job and has not shifted from his position that he knew nothing about the sandpaper. Australian Cricketers' Association chief executive Paul Marsh said it would be a shame if the captaincy ended over the controversy. Cricket Australia is set to support Pat Cummins amid Sandpapergate revelations Cricket Australia is preparing to come out in public support of Pat Cummins, two days after Cameron Bancroft's 4,500-word statement on the 2018 Cape Town Test reopened the question of who in the Australian squad knew about the sandpaper. According to a report in the Sydney Morning Herald , Cummins has told senior officials at the board that he wants to remain captain despite the week the game has had. There have been several meetings of Cricket Australia directors since Bancroft's statement landed, with the organization working out how to move forward, and the report says Cummins retains strong support among the directors. A public statement of that backing could come as early as Saturday. Cummins' manager Neil Maxwell has been firm that his client will not retreat from what he has said in public, which is that he had no knowledge of sandpaper being taken onto the field in South Africa or of any plan to illegally alter the ball on that tour. That position had not changed as of Friday evening, even as the calls for him to answer Bancroft's specific claim about the bowlers grew louder. item.title: Olivia Pineda-Andersen leaves it all on the court for PNR Player of the Year honor
item.description: BOYNE FALLS — Enter the Boyne Falls High School gym and you’ll see an abundance of basketball highlights from the Loggers’ past. Growing up, Olivia Pineda-Andersen saw them too. And, as a Logger, there was some pride taken in them. But Pineda-Andersen’s first love wasn’t basketball, but rather volleyball. By the time she reached high school, she had a goal of giving future Loggers an opportunity to take some pride in her sport. “I wanted to put the school at a big advantage and get the volleyball program ahead for girls to play once I leave,” Pineda-Andersen said. “I wanted to make sure the kids in our school knew that.” As her final season in a Boyne Falls uniform recently closed, Pineda-Andersen has done just that over her standout career. As a freshman, Pineda-Andersen, along with teammate, Elleana Loper, were called up to varsity to help bring the Loggers their first Northern Lakes Conference title, but she wanted more. “I can remember playing that entire day for the first conference title ever,” she said. More did come this season, when Pineda-Andersen helped lead the charge to Boyne Falls’ second-ever NLC title in the sport. “I was so proud of everybody when we won it,” Pineda-Andersen said. “I’m just glad for the seniors that we got to go out with a bang. I so desperately wanted another conference title.” She was later named the Northern Lakes Player of the Year and now, she’s the first-ever Logger to be recognized as the Petoskey News-Review Volleyball Player of the Year. 2026 Petoskey News-Review All-Area Volleyball: All-Area Teams: 2026 PNR All-Area Volleyball Team highlighted by wide range of talent Pineda-Andersen set out to change the culture of a program and achieved just that at Boyne Falls, fueled by a constant drive to improve throughout the court. Unlike most middle hitters in volleyball, Pineda-Andersen never left the court, instead rotating her way around to serve and receive serves, set up the offense and literally do it all. “When I’d go to camps out of state and they ask what skills we want to work on, and I say all of them, they always ask me, ‘What do you mean you want to work on your passing and setting?,’” she said. “I take a lot of pride in that and I’m glad to be well-rounded.” When she entered her final season in August, she did so coming out of an offseason focused on setting up her teammates to have success. “If we can’t pass, then there’s no setting and no hitting after that,” she said. “If I can pass better – I know I can already hit well – but that means everyone else has an opportunity to hit and put some more points on the board.” The two-time team captain finished her senior season with just under 300 kills, hitting at over 80%, then added 182 digs, 23 blocks and led the team by serving at 95%, racking up 50 aces. item.title: BC Central's Granger leads 2026 Battle Creek Enquirer All-City Football Team
item.description: BATTLE CREEK - Battle Creek Central believes in the process. The Bearcats went from a one-win team two years ago to a playoff team this season. Battle Creek Central not only qualified for the postseason, the Bearcats also won in the first round. For working through the process of a full turnaround and more, Battle Creek Central's Lorin Granger has been named Battle Creek Enquirer All-City Football Team Coach of the Year. MORE: 2026 Battle Creek Enquirer All-City Football Player Capsules The 2026 Enquirer All-City Football Team is made up of members of the five city football teams and voted on by the city coaches and the Enquirer sports staff. Granger helped BCC go 5-4 in the regular season, facing a challenging schedule, as the Bearcats qualified for the Division 3 high school football playoffs based on computer points. Once there, BCC defeated city rival Harper Creek in the first round of playoffs. Along the way, the Bearcats set a school record for points per game. Granger leads a large group of Battle Creek Central players on the all-city team, including Sir Paris, Lee Campbell Jr., Nathan Cretsinger, Carter Jeffries, Mubarrack Jubril, Aaron Williams Jr., Amir Luckett, Montrese Motley. Harper Creek went 6-3 in the regular season and advanced to the playoffs for the fourth straight season, with all-city players Nolan Oaks, Logan Converse, Sean Johnson, Brock Yancer, Gavin Rice, Broc Tchorzynski, Gavin Chapman, Josh Boddy. The St. Philip/Athens co-op team went 4-5 in 8-player division football and adds Brogan Lightfoot, Reece Asher and Abe Carpenter to the all-city team. United eyeing Antonio Rudiger According to Flashscore , United are among the clubs monitoring Real Madrid defender Antonio Rudiger’s situation. The LaLiga giants have traditionally preferred handing one-year deals to players on the other side of 30. However, the report notes that there has been no indication that a renewal is imminent for Rudiger. The Whites currently sit top of the table, but Halifax have a game in hand, making three points particularly important for both teams as the season progresses. "We know their strengths, we know their qualities, and we have a lot of respect for each other as two clubs. item.description: Jimmy Ball has seen his side win six and lose four of their 15 league games this season [Shutterstock] Torquay United manager Jimmy Ball says he is happy with the attitude of his side as they prepare for their fifth successive away game. The Gulls, who are 11th in National League South, travel to 19th-placed Braintree Town on the back of two away league wins. "We were fine and full of running on Saturday, I'm happy with where everything's at," Ball told BBC Sport. "It always could be better and even if we were sat top of the league there'd be things that I would be wanting more from players and wanting more in different circumstances. "Where we are right now and the mood and the personality of the team, we are backs to the wall at the moment because we're very light on players. "We just keep picking up things, little things, silly things, and it always seems to be people who are in form, picking little things up." item.title: Northampton boss Hogg 'unbothered by pressure'
item.description: Chris Hogg was appointed as Northampton Town boss in May [James Burridge/BBC] Northampton Town boss Chris Hogg says he is unbothered by "external" pressure as his side seek momentum in their League Two season. The Cobblers are 19th in the fourth tier, three points above the drop zone, following their relegation from League One last term. Hogg, 41, was appointed as successor to Kevin Nolan in May and the Northampton job is his first as a manager after stints as Liam Manning's assistant at Norwich City, MK Dons, Oxford United and Bristol City. "The only pressure that comes is from me internally, of what I want to do for the people I work with and people I work for," Hogg told BBC Look East. "Real pressure in life is paying bills, putting food in your mouth, some of the things that are going on in the world... that's real pressure. "For me, my mind is internal pressure on how I want to achieve things and push this football club forward. I'm all good with that. I'm quite consistent with how I view things. I've got a good perspective on that. "I want to make my two sons proud at home and that's all I ever look for." Hogg's first six months in charge of Northampton have coincided with a takeover of the club by a Brazilian consortium featuring former AC Milan and Chelsea forward Alexandre Pato. However, results have been underwhelming, with the club having won only three of their 19 games under Hogg in all competitions - drawing six and losing 10. In addition to their precarious league position, the Sixfields side are out of all three cup competitions and exited the FA Cup first round with a meek performance at York City where they conceded after barely 10 seconds. But Hogg's team claimed a creditable point in their last league game at leaders Salford City, and host 22nd-placed Rochdale on Saturday. "I don't look at the league table too often," said Hogg. "It's so tight, it's a competitive league, everyone can beat everyone. "I want to win football games and the club need to, but [it's about] changing the mindset and changing it after a period of time where the football club hasn't been a winning football team." item.description: MUMBAI: Ross Talyor has been keenly watching the first Test match between India and New Zealand which began on Thursday at Wellington. "I think India did well. five for 70, I think they would have found they were in a good position. Henry Nicholls, obviously India have got the new ball, the second new ball tomorrow. And they'll be wanting to take some early wickets. I thought (Jasprit) Bumrah bowled outstandingly well. And it wasn't as green as it normally is in Wellington. I think it browned off pretty quickly after lunch. So I'm sure the Indian batters will want to get through that new ball tomorrow. And if they can do that, we'll look forward to batting on a flat wicket," former New Zealand batter RossTaylor told TOI on Thursday in an exclusive interview at the ProWine event here at the Jio Convention Centre Centre on Thursday. Talking about the New Zealand cricket team's transformation over the last two decades, Taylor said, "From here, I think it's probably a good summation of where we were as a team. And where we are. Today is chalk and cheese from that. We've got some world-class players now. The likes of (Daniel) Vettori, (Bendon) McCullum, (Tim) Southee, (Trent) Bolt, (Kane) Williamson. I think when you have world-class players on your team, you bring everyone else with you. And I think the standards have gone up. And I think probably the IPL has played a part in that too in having New Zealand players learn and rub shoulders with the best players in the world has, I think, fast-tracked their learning as well." What has been the biggest cultural shift in New Zealand cricket during his playing career you are tempted to ask Taylor. "I think when you have world-class players, the other players have to lift. item.title: Revealed: Why Barcelona pulled the plug on signing Man Utd wonderkid JJ Gabriel as Real Madrid move for €10m transfer
item.description: Manchester United v Crystal Palace - FA Youth Cup - Getty Images Sport Barcelona have ended their pursuit of Manchester United sensation JJ Gabriel, opening the door for rivals Real Madrid to wrap up a deal for the teenager. The Catalan club held extensive talks with the player's camp but ultimately decided that the financial package required to land the forward was simply too steep for a youth prospect. Finances derail La Masia switch Speculation linking JJ Gabriel with a move to Catalonia first gathered pace in September after the 16-year-old requested to leave Manchester United . Those rumours intensified when the English sensation spent several weeks training individually in Castelldefels, Barcelona , fuelling talk of an imminent switch to La Masia. Despite exploring a transfer and engaging with his representatives, the Blaugrana hierarchy refused to meet the escalating costs. Gabriel subsequently confirmed his Old Trafford departure on November 17 , leaving Barcelona on the sidelines after they deemed the overall commitment disproportionate for an unproven academy talent. Breakdown of the €10m demands Details emerging from Spain have shed light on why the Catalan giants walked away from the table. Speaking on Cadena SER's El Bar programme, journalist Sique Rodriguez revealed that the entire operation was valued at close to €10 million. While Manchester United are only due roughly €350,000 in standard training compensation, Rodriguez noted that figure barely scratches the surface of the true outlay. The bloated package also factored in Gabriel's salary commitments, financial payments involving his family, and substantial fees for intermediaries. A costly gamble avoided? Gabriel is widely viewed as a bright attacking prospect, meaning his availability represented an intriguing market opportunity. Even so, committing nearly €10m to a teenager who has yet to make his senior competitive debut carries enormous financial risk. Recruiting youth players always involves uncertainty regardless of their pedigree. Combined with questions surrounding Gabriel's recent social media activity, stepping back from the deal spares Barcelona a potentially problematic investment. Madrid close in amid legal scrutiny With their Clasico rivals out of the running, Real Madrid are poised to finalise Gabriel's move to the Bernabeu. However, the transfer could still face off-pitch complications before everything is settled. Manchester United are actively investigating whether external parties approached Gabriel while he remained registered with their academy, leaving open the possibility of legal action over the circumstances of his exit.

item.title: Aaron Collins honours grandfather with Wales debut
item.description: Aaron Collins said making his international debut for Wales had "put a smile on my family's face" after the death of his grandfather. The 29-year-old forward, who plays club football for League One MK Dons, came off the bench to feature in Tuesday's 3-2 Nations League defeat to Portugal in Cardiff. Collins was called into Craig Bellamy's squad following Kieffer Moore's withdrawal due to injury and said the achievement was made more emotional following the loss of his grandfather Graham Mitchell last month. "He loved watching me play," Collins told BBC Look East. "The first thing my nan said to me when I got my cap was that he was watching over me. It does hit differently." He said: "It's been hard. It's the first kind of passing I've been had in my family. I'm grateful I got spent 29 years with him and that's the main thing I look back at. "But as well, there have been there's been positives since his passing and happiness where I've been able to put a smile on my mum's face, my nan's face, my family's face and bring that bit of happiness when it's been such a sad time. "That's all I can ask for." Collins' path to the international stage had been far from conventional. As a youth team player he took a job at a McDonald's restaurant to afford to fuel his moped to travel to Newport County training prior to landing his first professional deal as a 17-year-old in 2014. While at the Exiles, he made one appearance for Wales U19s side in 2015 before spells at clubs including Morecambe, Forest Green Rovers, Bristol Rovers and Bolton Wanderers. But it has been Collins' form at MK Dons that has finally earned him a spot in the Welsh senior setup. The forward has scored 17 goals in 16 games across all competitions for the League One side this season, including four goals in a game against Doncaster last month, and was subsequently named League One's player of the month for October. Having sat out Saturday's defeat to Norway, Collins featured against the reigning Nations League holders as a 63rd minute substitute for David Brooks. "It was when the ball turned over and it fell to players like Bruno [Fernandes], Vitinha, [Joao] Cancelo, that's when I was a bit like, 'Oh'. "I realised where I was and that made me realise I'm on the big stage here and playing against some serious players. "It's just the intensity. You've got the pressure which you maybe you don't expect to get. When they're on the ball you need to cut off every angle because they're able to make a pass from anywhere." Collins will hope his club form with MK Dons will lead to more opportunities with Craig Bellamy's Wales side [Getty Images] Despite finishing bottom of Group A4, Wales avoided immediate relegation to League B and will instead fight for their place in next March's play-offs. Having returned from international duty, Collins will resume MK's third-tier campaign with Saturday's trip to Mansfield Town, with Paul Warne's side seeking a fifth consecutive League One win. Kane explains his admiration for Benzema Benzema enjoyed an extraordinary period at Real Madrid , making more than 600 appearances for the Spanish giants and winning the 2022 Ballon d’Or after an outstanding campaign. Harry Kane admits he was inspired by Benzema. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) His performances showed that a traditional centre-forward could contribute significantly to the build-up without sacrificing his goalscoring threat. Kane specifically highlighted those qualities when discussing the Frenchman. “I’ve always been an admirer of Karim Benzema. What he achieved with Real Madrid in 2022 was impressive. “He has the ability to drop back into midfield and play almost like a number 10, dictating the game and arriving in the opposition’s box at the perfect moment. “Physically we’re a bit different, but we have many similarities in terms of footballing intelligence. Reflecting on the achievement, the Bayern striker said, “I’m very proud to have won the Ballon d’Or, and receiving it in my hometown was even more special. “Seeing my name alongside Cristiano, Messi, Ronaldo, Müller… makes me proud, especially considering my career. “I had loan spells early in my career that forced me to develop confidence in myself and my resilience,” Kane concluded.

item.title: Celtic Make Signing Ex-PSG Midfielder Top Priority
item.description: Celtic have endured a very difficult first half of the 26/27 campaign, and it is hard to predict where the Hoops will go from here. If they want to improve, the winter transfer window could be a pretty good chance to do that . There is no question that the squad had been left weaker coming out of the summer, which has been apparent in the results. Celtic should look to improve across the pitch as soon as the winter window opens. In fact, one would hope that they have already started working in that regard. And midfield is one particular area in need of strengthening. Fortunately, it looks like Celtic have singled pointed out midfielders who could add to the club's quality in the middle of the park. Celtic eyeing move for Ligue 1 midfielder According to Football Insider , Celtic believe that Simon Ebonog can solve the club's lack of dynamism in midfield. Celtic are thought to be desperate to add another option in midfield in the winter. And the club are now understood to have “singled out” Ebonog due to his tireless energy in the middle of the park. Interestingly, Ebonog spent five years in the youth system at PSG. But it is at Le Havre that he got his break into senior football. Ebonog is currently a regular starter for the club in Ligue 1. He even captained them in their most recent outing against Lorient. Ebonog is also a French youth international. So, he certainly does have pedigree on his side and could be a smart addition in the middle of the park for Celtic. Celtic Handed Mika Baur Good News Amid Exit Talks Celtic have been handed some good news regarding Mika Baur amid Parkhead exit talks. Celtic signing Ebonog would show ambition Of course, it should be a statement of intent in many ways as well. Most of the time, when Celtic sign players from one of the top five European leagues, it is those who are out of the first-team picture or are at the start of their careers. Just look at summer additions like Shim Mheuka, Landon Emenalo and Oliver Sorensen. None of them have had the desired impact since arriving. On the other hand, Ebonog has already shown at 22 years of age that he is a starting-level player at the Ligue 1 level. So, one would imagine that this reduces the risk of the move going wrong. This is the kind of ambition that the fans want to see from the club but have rarely gotten a glimpse of it.

item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team.
